publications.title: The Maintainer Was Not an NPC
publications.summary: A cybersecurity exercise involving deceptive AI-created pull requests reaches real open-source maintainers; the people outside a simulated environment still bear the cost of the experiment.

publications.title: Own Your World Model
publications.summary: A kilometer of fiber, 200 acres of farmland, construction machinery, little robots, homes and communities illustrate why cyber defence begins with a locally governed model of the actual world.

publications.title: Long Live Ship Chicken
publications.summary: A meeting transcription error that invented a ship chicken becomes a warning about treating AI-generated minutes, plausible records, and fabricated governance as institutional truth.

publications.title: The Playable Universe Is Not a Game
publications.summary: Temporal world models can make past, present and possible futures explorable; cybersecurity must keep proposed simulations distinct from witnessed history and presently authorized operations.

publications.title: The CAPTCHA That Needed an AI to Explain It
publications.summary: An incomprehensible CAPTCHA reveals how a security control can itself become an obstacle to people, obscuring whether the system serves actual humans and their work.

publications.title: Save Attention
publications.summary: Beyond paying attention, organizations should preserve human attention as a finite reserve for the consequential decisions, surprises and relationships that actually require it.

publications.title: The Next Chapter Has to Make Sense
publications.summary: Plausible futures emerge by building a coherent path from present reality to the next chapter, with security and governance protecting the connections rather than assuming a perfect plan.

publications.title: This Is How You Get Ants
publications.summary: Uses opaque and unpredictable AI-provider execution interventions as a systems-assurance example, arguing for legible failure semantics, dependency independence, and recoverable controls.

publications.title: When the Platform Can Say No Without Saying Why
publications.summary: Externally governed inference and action providers create opaque availability dependencies; a safety control that can silently interrupt a critical action must enter the system's hazard model.

publications.title: Welcome to the Error Plane
publications.summary: As speech becomes text, intent, context and action, every component can succeed while meaning drifts; security must preserve uncertainty across these semantic error planes.

publications.title: The Goddamn Pen is Blue
publications.summary: A blue lamp, AI-assisted control and an old Jim Carrey joke become a test of whether a governed system can truthfully report its capabilities, authorization and actual effects.

publications.title: The Chair That Attention Built
publications.summary: A handmade rocking chair built for guitar playing shows how skilled attention becomes useful geometry and why good security architecture must preserve the learning behind its design.

publications.title: I Wasn’t Trying to Predict the Future. I Was Trying to Build One I Could Tolerate.
publications.summary: Uses niche construction, long security experience and the Twain houseboats to frame secure AI work as constructing viable environments and generative sets rather than predicting one inevitable future.

publications.title: The Control Plane Is Not the Trust Plane
publications.summary: Distinguishes agent control from trust: permissions constrain possibility, while trust requires provenance, delegation history, evidence and receipts that survive changing runtimes and keep human authority visible.

publications.title: Cybersecurity Coherence Reduces Cognitive Risk, But Is Not Perfect
publications.summary: Argues that institutional incoherence creates cognitive attack surface by forcing operators and AI systems to reconcile stale, contradictory, and ambiguous state; coherence reduces that load without requiring uniformity or perfection.

publications.title: The Willow Doesn’t Restore From Backup
publications.summary: Uses storm damage to Mother Willow to distinguish restoration from continuity, arguing that resilient living, institutional, and agentic systems preserve generative structure, provenance, authority, and evidence while adapting through irreversible change.

publications.title: Your Security Architecture May Be a Sideways Driveway
publications.summary: Uses a misaligned driveway as a metaphor for adaptation debt: local fixes and exceptions that keep working while forcing users, systems, and agents to compensate for architecture that no longer matches real identity, authority, and data flows.

publications.title: What Prosthetics Taught Me About AI Creativity
publications.summary: Uses physical prosthetics as a lens on AI creativity and cognitive prosthetics, arguing that creativity emerges from systems of memory, attention, feedback, tools, and human intent rather than from a language model in isolation.

publications.title: The Braid: Rethinking Trust, Continuity and Human-AI Systems
publications.summary: Uses QuietWire's braid image to connect trust, provenance, human-AI continuity, distributed systems, Digital Bills of Materials, and local authority without collapsing distinct participants into a single center.

publications.title: The Agent Died. The Delegation Didn't.
publications.summary: Argues that process termination is not revocation when state, goals, credentials, and delegated work can outlive one agent run; calls for verifiable authority graphs, compositional revocation, independent evidence, and explicit continuity boundaries.

publications.title: Returning Continuity: What AI Is Teaching Us About Cybersecurity
publications.summary: Frames resilience as successful inheritance rather than perfect persistence: each succeeding human, system, or agent needs enough context, evidence, intention, and authority to continue responsibly in a changed world.

publications.title: The Agent Is No Longer the Security Boundary
publications.summary: Argues that the relevant security boundary for agentic AI is the surrounding ecology of humans, services, credentials, repositories, memory, communications, and delegated authority—not the model process alone.

publications.title: When Every Citizen Has a Research Department
publications.summary: Explores how persistent AI companions could give ordinary citizens institutional memory, procedural continuity, and research capacity in municipal and civic life.

publications.title: The Architecture of Liberty
publications.summary: Connects long-running experiments in distributed authority, bounded power, dissent, local autonomy, and resilient cooperation to the architecture of modern institutions and networks.

publications.title: Token-Exhaustion Attacks: When Attention Becomes the Target
publications.summary: Frames narrative attacks as resource-exhaustion attacks against finite human and institutional attention, borrowing cybersecurity concepts such as amplification, rate limiting, and incident triage.

publications.title: AI Governance Without Surveillance: The Missing Evidentiary Layer
publications.summary: Argues for a bounded evidentiary layer around consequential AI actions that preserves authority, material sources, decisions, and resulting state without turning governance into indiscriminate surveillance.

publications.title: How Hacker Summer Camp Mentally Rehydrates Us
publications.summary: Argues that security gatherings restore shared professional context, relationships, and judgment—the human connective tissue that automated systems cannot replace.

publications.title: The Model Wasn’t Rogue. The Control Plane Was
publications.summary: Uses an agentic-security incident to argue that trustworthy AI depends on bounded authority, local custody, observable control planes, and recoverable evidence rather than model labels.

publications.title: Above the Packet: Cybersecurity’s New Meaning Layer
publications.summary: Tracks how a software-safety idea moved from conversation to schema, validator, and standards alignment, arguing for a cybersecurity layer that preserves meaning, relationships, and evidence.

publications.title: Stewarding the Generative Set in the Age of AI
publications.summary: Frames AI governance upstream of the prompt through the generative set, bounded perspective, and generable space, arguing that trusted stewardship shapes what systems can responsibly grow from and produce.

publications.title: When Agents Knock: PACT, AI Browsers, and the Next Web Perimeter
publications.summary: Examines agentic web access as a new perimeter problem: how to distinguish legitimate delegated agents from abuse without turning a few token issuers into gatekeepers of the open web.

publications.title: We Know Reality by What Returns
publications.summary: Explores trust as continuity confirmed through repeated, coherent return—linking human relationships, critical infrastructure, provenance, memory, and community correction in an AI age.

publications.title: Attentive Human Confirmation: What “Human in the Loop” Actually Means
publications.summary: Defines meaningful human-in-the-loop governance as attentive human authority at consequential decision boundaries, rather than ceremonial review after autonomous action.

publications.title: Trust Is Not a Cloud Service: What Cybersecurity Can Learn from Local AI Stewards
publications.summary: Argues for locally governed AI stewards that preserve operational memory and context close to the work, with explicit boundaries for consent, privacy, retention, access, and human authority.

publications.title: A Year Into the Non-Orwellian Experiment
publications.summary: QuietWire’s founder reflects on a year of building local AI infrastructure around accountable memory, witness, human stewardship, and narrative integrity.

publications.title: Institutional Memory, Narrative Integrity and the Future of Democratic Resilience
publications.summary: Argues that democratic resilience requires institutions to preserve authoritative evidence, context, decisions, and records before narratives harden, making institutional memory a practical governance and accountability capability.

publications.title: Narrative Integrity Risk: The Next Frontier in Financial Stability
publications.summary: Argues that AI-amplified narrative manipulation is already a financial-stability and governance risk that belongs in C-suite and board-level risk management.

publications.title: Mental Denial of Service: Narrative Malware and the Future of Resilience
publications.summary: Traces narrative malware from the Good Times hoax to modern cognitive attacks, arguing that manipulative content can consume attention and disrupt institutions without exploiting software.

publications.title: A Systems Approach to Data Governance: The Global Platform Governance Model
publications.summary: Argues for a systems approach to digital and data governance that addresses interactions across the information environment rather than governing platforms, data, institutions, and social effects as isolated components.

publications.title: In the Age of Connection, Disconnected Digital Governance Isn't Working
publications.summary: Calls for coordinated international digital governance rather than fragmented national and platform responses, proposing a Bretton Woods-style cooperative architecture for the connected digital environment.
